history.period: 1661 AD (disputed — some sources say 19th century; verify)
history.summary: CSV town 'Ambassa' is wrong and has been corrected: no Jagannath Bari is documented at Ambassa (Dhalai district) despite genuine searching. The best-supported referent for the name 'Jagannath Bari' in Tripura is the famous Vaishnava temple at Palace Compound, Krishna Nagar, Agartala (23.836318, 91.280536), near Ujjayanta Palace — documented with identity uncertainty flagged. It enshrines Jagannath with Balabhadra and Subhadra and is known for its annual Rath Yatra; the structure has an octagonal base with pillars crowned by square and pyramidal cones. FOUNDING-DATE CONFLICT: Odisha Sun Times reports it was built in 1661 AD by Maharaja Govinda Manikya, while Wanderlog and travel guides attribute it to the 19th century under Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya — unresolved, needs verification. Generic travel blogs list a 'Jagannath Temple' among Ambassa attractions but describe it generically (four-storey shrine of Jagannath-Balabhadra-Subhadra) and appear to conflate it with the Agartala temple; no Ambassa-specific Jagannath temple could be verified.

name: Jagannath Bari
town_description: Agartala is the capital city of Tripura in West Tripura district; Jagannath Bari stands at Palace Compound, Krishna Nagar, near Ujjayanta Palace.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~12 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Rath Yatra (June-July) is the main festival
